tasks.title: Implement LRU cache in config.ts
tasks.description: Add inline LRU caching mechanism to src/config.ts to cache config file reads. This improves performance and enables safe parallelization of findConfigFiles.
tasks.details:
Currently config.ts has no caching and performs sequential scanning (lines 79-97). Implement an LRU cache using either:

Option A: Simple Map-based LRU (no new dependencies)
- Use Map with insertion order tracking
- Implement size limit and TTL
- ~15 lines of code

Option B: Use lru-cache npm package
- Install `lru-cache` v11+
- Leverage built-in TTL and size limits
- More feature-rich

Recommendation: Start with simple Map-based LRU to avoid new dependencies. Cache key: normalized config path. Cache value: parsed config with timestamp.

Integration points:
- readJsoncFile: check cache first
- findConfigFiles: cache directory listings
- Invalidate on writes (backupConfig already creates new files)
tasks.testStrategy: Add tests for LRU cache behavior: eviction, TTL expiry, hit/miss rates. Benchmark performance improvement. Verify cache invalidation on config writes.

tasks.title: Add deprecation patterns to agentSystem.ts
tasks.description: Add proper deprecation annotations and migration guides to deprecated exports in src/agentSystem.ts. Include JSDoc @deprecated tags with @see alternatives.
tasks.details:
agentSystem.ts contains deprecated exports that cause DRY violations. Instead of removing them immediately, add proper deprecation patterns:

1. Add JSDoc @deprecated tags
2. Include @see references to replacement APIs
3. Consider runtime warnings (once per session)
4. Document migration path in code comments

Example:
```typescript

 * @deprecated Use getAgentSystem() instead. This wrapper will be removed in v2.0.
 * @see getAgentSystem()
 */

```

This provides backward compatibility while guiding users to modern APIs.

tasks.title: Add configuration caching mechanism
tasks.description: Enhance config.ts with a proper caching layer that invalidates on file changes. This is an extension of the LRU cache (task 6) with file watching capabilities.
tasks.details:
Beyond the basic LRU cache, add intelligent cache invalidation:

1. Track file modification times (mtime)
2. Invalidate cache entries when source files change
3. Optional: use fs.watch for real-time invalidation (careful with performance)
4. Add cache statistics (hit rate, size)

Implementation:
- Cache key: config file path
- Cache value: { data: Config, mtime: number, expires: number }
- On read: check mtime, invalidate if changed
- On write: explicitly invalidate

This prevents stale config reads while maintaining performance.
tasks.testStrategy: Test cache invalidation by modifying config files. Verify stale data is not served. Benchmark cache hit rates. Test edge cases: file deleted, permissions changed, etc.

tasks.title: Optimize I/O using Bun.file() where applicable
tasks.description: Review config.ts and other I/O-heavy modules to use Bun.file() instead of Node fs for better performance. This leverages Bun's optimized file I/O.
tasks.details:
Bun provides optimized file I/O via Bun.file(). Review the codebase for fs.readFileSync, fs.readFile, fs.writeFileSync, etc. and replace with Bun equivalents where beneficial:

- fs.readFileSync → Bun.file(path).text() or .json()
- fs.writeFileSync → Bun.write(path, data)

Considerations:
- Bun.file() returns promises by default
- Better performance for large files
- Native TypeScript support (no transpile)
- Keep backward compatibility if needed

Focus on hot paths: config loading, backup creation, file scanning.
tasks.testStrategy: Benchmark I/O performance before/after. Verify file operations still work correctly. Test error handling (file not found, permissions).
